sources.cite: Microsoft Learn (Azure China mirror), Diagnose and troubleshoot Azure Cosmos DB request rate too large (429) exceptions
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: a 429 means requests 'are being rate limited' when they exceed the provisioned RU/s in a second; throughput is split evenly across physical partitions (normalized RU consumption per PartitionKeyRangeId); the SDKs 'automatically retry requests on 429s', typically up to nine times; raising RU/s temporarily 'isn't recommended as a long-term strategy'; 'The partition key can't be updated in place', so changing it means moving data to a new container. The Cosmos DB page 'Query performance tips for Azure Cosmos DB SDKs' (read 2026-11-18): 'Cross-partition queries require the SDK to visit all existing partitions to check for results. The more physical partitions the container has, the slower they can potentially be'; targeting the partition key in the query options makes a single-partition query.

brief.situation: You are the developer at Corvin Garden Supply. The orders container in Cosmos DB for NoSQL is partitioned by /customerId (24 physical partitions, 20,000 RU/s). This morning's release added a 'my orders' panel. Since 09:50 checkout writes to the same container fail with 429 after retries and the account page is slow. The spring sale email goes out at 11:00.
handover: The panel's query is SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.customerId = @id ORDER BY c.created DESC.
RU/s can be raised in minutes; changing the partition key needs a new container and a migration.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the container's physical partitions, the panel's query and checkout's writes.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The sale email goes out at 11:00, 45 minutes after the page.

writeup.question: For the record: why checkout was throttled, what you changed, and why not a new partition key.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Reads RU per partition and per query.
parts.modelAnswer: Since the release all 24 partitions were at 100% normalized RU. The panel's query cost about 72 RU because the SDK call set enable_cross_partition_query and no partition key, so it fanned out to every partition.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: partition_key=customer_id in the query call (about 3 RU, one partition), deployed, with RU/s raised to 30,000 only until the deploy and then reverted.

parts.label: Not a new key
parts.criteria: Knows the partition key was right.
parts.modelAnswer: /customerId already matches the query. Recreating the container would have deleted the orders, and /orderId would make this query fan out. A test now requires single-partition account queries, and 429s alert.

expertPath.text: All ranges 100% since 09:50; query 72 RU across 24 partitions; no partition_key in the call; index fine.
Pass partition_key; temporary 30,000 RU/s; deploy; test and alert.

containerGone.headline: Fix the query, not the container
containerGone.body: The partition key already matched the query. The SDK call simply did not pass it. A partition key change needs a new container and a migration, and it was not the problem.

saleThrottled.headline: A filter in the text is not a partition key
saleThrottled.body: Give the SDK the partition key so a query goes to one partition. Without it, every load costs RUs on every partition.

singlePartition.headline: Good: read the RU charge
singlePartition.body: You saw every partition saturated since the release, measured the query's fan-out and charge, passed the partition key, bridged with a temporary RU increase, checked, and guarded with a test and an alert.

scoring.modelReasoning: Every physical partition is saturated since the release, and the new query costs about 72 RU because the SDK call does not pass the partition key, so it fans out to all 24 partitions. Pass customerId as the partition key so each query goes to one partition, bridge with a short RU increase until the deploy, then revert. Recreating the container deletes data and the key is already right; more SDK retries only hide throttling. Add a test and a 429 alert.
